title: queue.rs: .env written after .msg but both in same directory — drain can process .msg before .env exists
description: queue.rs NntpQueue::enqueue: the .msg file is written and renamed first, then the .env is written. drain_once scans for .msg files and reads the paired .env. Between the .msg rename and the .env rename there is a window where drain_once can pick up the .msg, fail to find the .env (NotFound branch), and proceed with stoa_core::default_injection_source() — silently losing the injection source. This is a TOCTOU race between enqueue and drain_once. The drain comment says 'If no .env exists the drain skips .msg files that have no paired .env' but the code at queue.rs line 223 does NOT skip: it calls stoa_core::default_injection_source() and proceeds to deliver the article. So in the window between the two renames, the article gets delivered with the wrong injection source, and then the .env arrives — the .msg has already been deleted after delivery, leaving an orphaned .env file. The orphaned .env will never be cleaned up by cleanup_orphan_msg_files (which only handles .msg without .env, not .env without .msg).
